review_comment: The async_run function executes shell commands by concatenating directory-listed executables with client-provided metadata without neutralization of shell metacharacters. Client-controlled hostname, profile, and groups values can contain characters like semicolons or backticks to inject arbitrary commands. Replace os.system() with subprocess.run() using a list of arguments, or at minimum validate metadata values against a strict allowlist of safe characters before shell execution.

The added code executes notifier scripts with client-supplied metadata as arguments via shell command without validation. Client-controlled hostname, profile, or group names containing shell metacharacters could enable arbitrary command execution. Use subprocess.call() with explicit argument list instead of os.system() to avoid shell interpretation, or implement strict input validation that rejects shell metacharacters in metadata values.

The code constructs executable paths from directory listing entries without validating for path traversal sequences. If malicious filenames containing '../' sequences can be written to the spool directory, they could execute arbitrary commands outside the intended directory. Validate and sanitize all filenames from directory listings using os.path.normpath() and ensure they remain within the intended directory before execution.
